# Template — Pilot Letter of Intent (LOI) Agreement

> ⚠️ **Template only.** Starting point for discussions, not legal advice.
> Review by a lawyer before signature. Fill every `[bracket]`. Use with
> `docs/OFFER-EUDR-READINESS-2026.md` and `docs/PILOT-OUTREACH-2026.md`.
> Works for all three pilot tracks — mark the applicable one in §2.

**Pilot title:** `[e.g. EUDR geo-trace pilot — Lobatse export chain group]`
**LOI date:** `[date]`

## Parties
1. **AgriSphere operator:** `[legal entity name, registration no., address, contact person, phone/email]` ("Platform")
2. **Pilot partner:** `[organisation, registration no./TIN if any, address, contact person, phone/email]` ("Partner")

## 1. Purpose
The parties intend to test, for a fixed period, the use of the AgriSphere
geo-trace & compliance workspace in the Partner's real supply chain, to
learn together whether it reduces the cost of export-readiness
documentation, and to decide on a possible paid service. This LOI records
that intention; it is **not** an exclusive agreement and does **not** commit
either party to a purchase.

## 2. Pilot track (mark one)
- [ ] **A — Export chain:** Partner is an exporter/abattoir/processor
  (or co-ordinator of one); pilot covers `[supplier group, product line,
  e.g. ranches supplying line X for EU-destined beef]`.
- [ ] **B — Co-op / union workspace:** Partner is a co-operative, union or
  producer association; pilot covers `[member group size, product]` with
  members sharing holdings into pooled lots.
- [ ] **C — Evidence & programme partner:** Partner is an insurer, input
  company, NGO or programme (e.g. index-insurance evidence kits, input
  programmes); pilot covers `[use case]`.

## 3. Pilot scope (what the Platform will deliver)
1. A hosted workspace for the pilot group with: consent-first holding
   records (coordinates), consignment lots with holding chains, and
   self-declared readiness exports (CSV/JSON) — live functionality of the
   AgriSphere platform as at the date of this LOI.
2. Format engineering: export layout aligned to `[the buyer's / Partner's
   compliance team's]` requirements, agreed in week 1 of the pilot.
3. Training & support: `[e.g. one onboarding session + office-hours
   channel]` for the pilot duration.
4. Honest documentation: each export carries the self-declared disclaimer
   (not a certificate, not a TRACES due-diligence statement); no
   certification or compliance assurance is sold or implied.

## 4. What the Partner will deliver
1. A named pilot lead and `[e.g. 60 minutes per month]` for checkpoints.
2. Access to a real pilot group: `[describe: e.g. 8–15 ranches/co-op
   members]` that consent to participating.
3. Real requirements: `[e.g. one buyer's data-request template]` to shape
   the export format.
4. Honest feedback at each checkpoint, including what does not work.

## 5. Data, consent & privacy
1. All personal and geo data is recorded **only with each producer's
   explicit consent**, and each producer controls which accounts may use
   their records (revocable at any time through the platform).
2. The Partner may read/export only records shared with it; the Platform
   enforces this in code.
3. The parties will sign the Platform's Data Processing Agreement
   (`docs/templates/DATA-PROCESSING-AGREEMENT.md`) before any personal data
   is processed under this pilot.
4. Neither party sells or monetises the other's data; published insights
   are aggregate-only and contain no raw text or personal data.

## 6. Term, cost & decision point
1. Pilot term: `[e.g. 12 weeks]` from `[start date]`.
2. Fees: `[e.g. free pilot; Partner pays only its own costs — or agreed
   fee P·]`. Farmers/producers in the pilot pay nothing.
3. Decision point: at week `[12]` the parties discuss a paid service under
   the Platform's standard pricing `[price envelope: see offer §6]`; either
   party may walk away without penalty.
4. Either party may end the pilot early with `[·]` days' written notice;
   data-return/deletion per the DPA applies on exit.

## 7. No exclusivity — intellectual property
1. This LOI grants no exclusivity. Each party remains free to work with
   others, including competing pilots.
2. Each party keeps its pre-existing IP. Improvements to the Platform made
   during the pilot belong to the Platform (the Platform's public code
   remains open-source where it is). Reports and learnings may be published
   only by mutual written consent, and any publication will name the pilot
   only with the Partner's permission.

## 8. Honesty clause
Neither party will state publicly that the pilot "certifies", "approves" or
"guarantees" any product, producer, chain or compliance outcome. Public
claims are limited to: the pilot is testing documentation infrastructure
for export readiness.

## 9. Governing law
`[Botswana / ·]` law; courts of `[·]`. [Adapt after professional review.]
